stories.title: NextDC warns of data centre delay amid power supply crunch
stories.summary: Power supplies to NextDC’s controversial M3 data centre expansion in Melbourne had been delayed, the developer said on Monday, as trading in its shares was halted pending an update on the potential…
stories.why_it_matters: A power supply delay at a flagship NextDC facility signals that grid constraints are now directly hitting project timelines for Australia's largest independent data centre operator. Investors face earnings uncertainty, hyperscale and colocation customers planning capacity in Melbourne may need to reassess delivery dates, and utilities and regulators come under renewed pressure to accelerate power infrastructure for the sector.
stories.content:
Power supplies to NextDC’s controversial M3 data centre expansion in Melbourne had been delayed, the developer said on Monday, as trading in its shares was halted pending an update on the potential hit to its balance sheet.

The company’s M3 data centre in West Footscray, used to process artificial intelligence services, is located just 15 metres away from some homes and has drawn complaints from local residents about noise levels, emissions and new electricity infrastructure.

stories.title: Aussie founder’s $50b float at risk as Microsoft axes data centre deal
stories.summary: Microsoft has pulled out of a major data centre deal in a blow to Australian entrepreneur Joshua Payne’s plans for a multibillion-dollar listing with his UK data centre developer Nscale.
stories.content:
Microsoft has pulled out of a major data centre deal in a blow to Australian entrepreneur Joshua Payne’s plans for a multibillion-dollar listing with his UK data centre developer Nscale.

The US tech giant, one of Nscale’s two largest customers, recently informed the company that it was pulling the plug on its agreement, which was announced last year.

stories.title: PM: Malaysia must plan data centre growth to attract quality investments
stories.summary: KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 19): Malaysia must strategically plan the growth of its data centre industry to attract quality investments, strengthen the digital economy and ensure the sustainable use of energy and water while protecting the environment, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
stories.why_it_matters: The comments signal that Malaysia's government is moving from welcoming all data centre investment toward a more selective, sustainability-linked policy stance. Developers and hyperscalers planning capacity in Johor and the Klang Valley should anticipate tighter scrutiny on power and water consumption, which could reshape site selection, project approvals, and operating costs across one of APAC's fastest-growing hubs.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 19): Malaysia must strategically plan the growth of its data centre industry to attract quality investments, strengthen the digital economy and ensure the sustainable use of energy and water while protecting the environment, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.

He said infrastructure readiness, energy supply and resource-use efficiency required closer scrutiny as the country sought to develop the industry sustainably.

Anwar said this in a post on X, after chairing the National Economic Action Council (MTEN) meeting on Monday.

The meeting also reviewed the Circular Economy Framework (RKEK), which aims to improve resource efficiency, reduce waste and promote the reuse of products and materials for as long as possible before they become waste.

“Effective coordination across sectors, ministries and agencies is needed to ensure the circular economy approach is implemented comprehensively and sustainably,” he said.

stories.title_zh: 马来西亚总理：须规划数据中心发展以吸引优质投资
stories.summary_zh: 吉隆坡（10月19日）：马来西亚总理Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim表示，马来西亚必须战略性地规划其数据中心产业的发展，以吸引优质投资、壮大数字经济，并在保护环境的同时确保能源和水资源的可持续利用。
stories.why_zh: 这些言论表明，马来西亚政府正从欢迎一切数据中心投资转向更具选择性、与可持续发展挂钩的政策立场。计划在柔佛和巴生谷建设容量的开发商和hyperscaler应预见到电力和水资源消耗将受到更严格的审查，这可能会重塑这一亚太地区增长最快的枢纽之一的选址、项目审批和运营成本格局。

stories.title: Australia's NEXTDC halts share trading before update on data centre power delay
stories.summary: BENGALURU (Oct 19): Australia's NEXTDC on Monday said its shares had been placed on a trading halt pending a market update it will provide on the impact of a delay in power supply to its M3 Melbourne data centre.
stories.why_it_matters: A formal trading halt underscores that the M3 power delay is material enough to require disclosure under listing rules, rather than a routine construction slip. The forthcoming update will set expectations for NEXTDC's expansion pipeline and could ripple across valuations of other APAC data centre developers exposed to similar power connection risks.

sources.name: The Edge Malaysia — data centre search

stories.content:
BENGALURU (Oct 19): Australia's NEXTDC on Monday said its shares had been placed on a trading halt pending a market update it will provide on the impact of a delay in power supply to its M3 Melbourne data centre.

The data centre operator said it expects to make an announcement within two days, adding that its board is yet to meet to assess the delay and its implications.

Analysts at Citi said that the delay likely relates to electricity distributor Jemena pausing work on electricity lines meant to deliver power to M3.

That would likely delay the billing from M3, which represents around 70 megawatts (MW) of the 155 MW of incremental billing in the state of Victoria the brokerage assumed for fiscal year 2027, it added.

NEXTDC said the trading halt would allow the company to meet its continuous disclosure obligations while it evaluates the impact of the power supply delay, including any potential effect on its fiscal 2027 financial guidance.

In August, the company forecast underlying earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation for fiscal 2027 to be between A$385 million and A$410 million (US$268.27 million to US$285.69 million).

Citi said that while it is likely the whole billing capacity for M3 is not impacted, the delay could put at risk around A$25 million in NEXTDC's operating earnings for fiscal 2027.

stories.title_zh: 澳大利亚 NEXTDC 在发布数据中心电力延期更新前停牌
stories.summary_zh: 班加罗尔（10月19日）：澳大利亚NEXTDC周一表示，其股票已停牌，等待公司就其M3墨尔本数据中心供电延迟的影响向市场发布更新。
stories.why_zh: 正式停牌凸显了M3供电延迟的重大程度——已足以触发上市规则下的信息披露要求，而非普通的施工延误。即将发布的更新将为NEXTDC的扩建管线设定预期，并可能波及亚太地区其他面临类似电力并网风险的数据中心开发商的估值。

stories.title: GreenSquare SYD1 opens first stage after adaptive reuse of 1995 data center
stories.summary: Australian data center operator GreenSquare today announced that the first stage of its SYD1 data centre campus in Norwest Business Park, Western Sydney, is now operational, following the adaptive reuse of a data center originally opened in 1995. The AI-ready data center was completed and ready for service in eight months with Australian neocloud Sharon AI […]
stories.content:
Australian data center operator GreenSquare today announced that the first stage of its SYD1 data centre campus in Norwest Business Park, Western Sydney, is now operational, following the adaptive reuse of a data center originally opened in 1995.

The AI-ready data center was completed and ready for service in eight months with Australian neocloud Sharon AI being its first customer. Sharon AI is deploying approximately 8,200 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs, a significant deployment of NVIDIA HGX B300 infrastructure in Australia.

GreenSquare retained the existing slab and much of the structure rather than demolishing and rebuilding. The data halls were relocated to the ground floor, to accommodate latest-generation, high-density compute without additional structural reinforcement. This increased IT capacity by 275 per cent while substantially reducing structural carbon.

SYD1 has a projected power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.20 and potable water usage effectiveness (WUE) of less than 0.1 litres per kilowatt-hour, both below the NSW Government guideline benchmarks of 1.25 and 1.0, respectively. It uses a closed-loop cooling system and rainwater harvesting.

An independent assessment by engineering consultants TTW found that the adaptive reuse retained 92 per cent of the building’s existing structural carbon. Combined with low-carbon concrete, it resulted in 76 per cent lower structural upfront carbon per square metre and 93 per cent lower carbon per kilowatt of IT capacity compared with a new-build facility.

Main construction works began in February 2026 with more than 350,000 hours of work recorded without a lost-time injury. About 400 people worked on site at peak time with teams operating around the clock during critical stages of the construction.

The NSW Government’s Investment Delivery Authority has endorsed a proposed 80 MW second stage. GreenSquare is backed by programs managed by Partners Group.

GreenSquare Chief Technology Officer, Joshua Martens, said: “We saw an opportunity to give a 30-year-old data centre a completely new purpose. By rethinking the building’s configuration, introducing prefabricated systems design, and using the latest technology to reduce carbon, we’ve created a facility that can support some of today’s most demanding compute requirements while using resources far more efficiently.”
